Last bánh mì (Bà Huynh this time)

picks.name: Cu Chi Tunnels + shooting range
picks.what: Crawl the tunnels, then fire an AK or M60 at the range. Go to Bến Dược if you can: bigger and quieter than Bến Đình, where every tour bus goes. Leave early to beat the crowds and bring earplugs.
picks.price: entry, range is extra (about ₫350k for 10 rounds)

picks.name: War Remnants Museum
picks.what: Vietnam War history. Heavy going, about two hours.
picks.map: War Remnants Museum Ho Chi Minh City

picks.name: Independence Palace
picks.what: A 1960s time capsule. Tanks on the lawn, war rooms and bunkers in the basement.
picks.map: Independence Palace Ho Chi Minh City

picks.name: Central Post Office
picks.what: French-era post office that's still working. Send a postcard home from it. The cathedral's right next door.

picks.name: Night street food tour on the back of a motorbike
picks.what: A local rides you around the districts you'd never find on your own, four or five food stops and a beer.

picks.name: Chợ Lớn (Chinatown)
picks.what: Bình Tây Market and the incense-filled Thiên Hậu temple.

picks.name: Bánh Mì Huỳnh Hoa
picks.what: The famous overloaded one. There'll be a queue and it's pricier than most, but do it once.

picks.name: Bánh Mì Bà Huynh
picks.what: Shorter queue, and some reckon it's better than Huỳnh Hoa.
picks.map: Banh Mi Ba Huynh 185 Cong Quynh

picks.name: Cơm tấm (broken rice)
picks.what: Grilled pork chop on broken rice with a fried egg. Saigon's everyday meal. Cơm Tấm Sà Bì Chưởng gets packed at dinner.

picks.name: Phở Tàu Bay
picks.what: One of the oldest phở shops in the city, well off the tourist trail.

picks.name: Xóm Chiếu Market
picks.what: Early morning food market in District 4, open about 4–11am. Go on the first morning while you're jet-lagged anyway.

picks.name: Bùi Viện Walking Street
picks.what: Backpacker chaos: speakers, shisha, buckets, fire breathers. Do it once. Two hours is plenty. Phones go missing in the crush, so keep yours in a front pocket.

picks.name: Pub Crawl Saigon
picks.what: Five bars and a club, free shots, starts around 8:30pm. Easy way to meet people on night one.

picks.name: Chill Skybar
picks.what: 26th floor rooftop with 360° views. Smart casual, so no thongs or singlets. Cocktails are dear; go for sunset happy hour.

picks.name: Social Club Rooftop
picks.what: 24th floor pool bar with the best District 1 skyline view. Also smart casual.

picks.name: Banana Mama
picks.what: Cheaper rooftop right above Bùi Viện. Good for watching the chaos below with a beer.

picks.name: The Café Apartments, 42 Nguyễn Huệ
picks.what: Old apartment block where every flat is now a café. The front of it is all over Instagram. Pay a few thousand đồng for the lift.

picks.name: Landmark 81
picks.what: Tallest building in Vietnam. The bar on floors 75–76 has the widest view over the city and river.

picks.name: Nguyễn Huệ Walking Street
picks.what: Wide pedestrian boulevard that fills up after dark with buskers and kids on hoverboards.

tips: Grab is the easiest way to get around. Airport to District 1 is 30–45 minutes.
Snatch-and-grab from motorbikes happens. Hold your phone on the footpath side, not the road side.
Rooftop bars want smart casual. Pack one pair of proper shoes.

days.title: Into the hills
items: Arrive early, find coffee, nap
Crazy House
Alpine Coaster at Datanla
Night market: bánh tráng nướng and hot soy milk
100 Roofs (the Maze Bar)

days.title: Canyoning
items: Full day canyoning at Datanla, lunch included
Chicken hot pot (lẩu gà lá é) to warm up

days.title: Clouds, then coast
items: Optional 4:30am run to Cầu Đất tea hill for the sea of clouds
Bánh căn for breakfast
Minibus to Nha Trang

picks.name: Canyoning at Datanla
picks.what: Abseil down waterfalls, cliff jumps, natural slides and the famous 'washing machine'. Only book a licensed operator: Highland Sport Travel, Phat Tire Ventures or Viet Challenge. Lunch and gear are included.

picks.name: Datanla Alpine Coaster
picks.what: A bobsled through the forest that you control yourself. Short but good fun. Go early, the queues get long on weekends.

picks.name: White-water rafting
picks.what: Grade II–III rapids on the Đồng Nai River, about 45 minutes out. Fine for first-timers.

picks.name: Cầu Đất tea hill at sunrise
picks.what: 'Cloud hunting': tea rows and wind turbines above a sea of cloud. It's 25 km out, so leave by 4:30am. Freezing at the top.

picks.name: Lang Biang mountain
picks.what: The local peak. Hike it or take the jeep up for the view over the valley.

picks.name: Bánh tráng nướng
picks.what: 'Vietnamese pizza': rice paper grilled over coals with egg, spring onion and chilli. Da Lạt invented it. Get it at the night market.

picks.name: Lẩu gà lá é
picks.what: Chicken hot pot with a peppery local herb. There's a good one at 9 Huỳnh Thúc Kháng.
picks.map: lau ga la e 9 Huynh Thuc Khang Da Lat

picks.name: Bánh căn
picks.what: Mini rice pancakes cooked in clay moulds and dunked in sauce. The stall at 7 Tăng Bạt Hổ is the one.
picks.map: Banh can 7 Tang Bat Ho Da Lat

picks.name: 100 Roofs Café (the Maze Bar)
picks.what: A bar built like a rabbit warren: tunnels, staircases and hidden rooms. Check the address on Google Maps first.

picks.name: Night market
picks.what: Starts around 6pm. Hot soy milk, grilled skewers, cheap jumpers. Bring cash.

picks.name: Crazy House
picks.what: Gaudí meets Alice in Wonderland. Twisting staircases over the rooftops. Da Lạt's most-posted spot.

tips: Nights drop to about 10–12°C. Pack a jumper and long pants.
Canyoning means you'll be soaked all day. Wear shoes that can get wet and leave the phone at the hostel.

days.title: Slow day

Last beach session

picks.name: Island hopping and snorkelling at Hòn Mun
picks.what: A day boat round the islands with a stop at the Hòn Mun marine reserve, the best snorkelling near town. Check the operator actually goes to Hòn Mun.

picks.name: Surf at Bãi Dài
picks.what: Long Beach, 30 minutes south. January waves are small and friendly, so it's good for learning. Nha Trang Local Surf School and Single Fin both teach in English. Watch the rips.
picks.map: Bai Dai Beach Nha Trang surf

picks.name: Night squid fishing
picks.what: Head out at sunset, drop lines under the lights, and eat what you catch for dinner. Shared boats are cheap. Weather can cancel it.
picks.price: shared boat from about US$20 each

picks.name: Mud bath
picks.what: Wallow in warm mud, then hot springs and pools. Tháp Bà is on the mainland; Hòn Tằm is on an island and comes with a beach.

picks.name: VinWonders
picks.what: Theme park and water park on Hòn Tre island. The ticket includes the 3 km cable car over the sea.

picks.name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
picks.what: Brick temple towers over 1,000 years old, on a hill over the river mouth. Quick visit.

picks.name: Nem nướng
picks.what: Grilled pork sausage you wrap in rice paper with herbs. Nha Trang's signature. Đặng Văn Quyên is always full of locals.
picks.map: Nem nuong Dang Van Quyen Nha Trang

picks.name: Bún cá
picks.what: Fish noodle soup with jellyfish. Proper Nha Trang breakfast. Try Bún Cá Nguyên Loan, 123 Ngô Gia Tự.
picks.map: Bun ca Nguyen Loan Nha Trang

picks.name: Seafood, one street back
picks.what: The beachfront on Trần Phú charges double. Walk a block or two inland and pick it live from the tanks.

picks.name: Sailing Club
picks.what: Beach restaurant by day, beach club by night. Shoes in the sand, music late.

picks.name: Skylight
picks.what: Rooftop beach club on the 45th floor of the Havana hotel. Big views over the bay.

picks.name: Cable car to Hòn Tre
picks.what: One of the longest over-sea cable cars anywhere.

tips: Water's clearest in the middle of the year. In January it can be a bit murky after rain, so pick a calm day for snorkelling.
Hostels sell boat days and mud-bath trips cheaper than the beachfront agents.

Bánh Mì Phượng

Tailor fitting
Madam Khánh to settle the bánh mì debate
Cao lầu for dinner

days.title: Last morning together
items: Old Town before 9am while it's empty
Pick up the tailoring
Three fly home, four head to Đà Nẵng

picks.name: Old Town at night and a lantern boat
picks.what: The whole town lights up after dark. Buy a boat ride from the official booths on either riverbank (not the people who come up to you) and float a candle lantern.

picks.name: Old Town ticket
picks.what: Covers the Japanese Bridge and a few old houses and museums. Walk it before 9am, when the tour groups take over.

picks.name: Bikes to An Bàng Beach
picks.what: Ride out through the rice paddies and the Trà Quế veggie village to the beach. Most stays have free bikes.

picks.name: Basket boats in the coconut forest
picks.what: Round bamboo boats that the rowers spin like a teacup ride. Touristy, but a laugh.
picks.map: Cam Thanh coconut forest basket boat

picks.name: Get something tailored
picks.what: Suits and shirts made to measure in a day or two. You need two fittings, so go on the first morning (27 Jan).

picks.name: Bánh mì showdown
picks.what: Bánh Mì Phượng (2B Phan Châu Trinh) vs Madam Khánh, 'the Bánh Mì Queen' (115 Trần Cao Vân).

picks.name: Cao lầu
picks.what: Chewy noodles you can only properly get in Hội An. Thanh Cao Lầu on Thái Phiên Street.

picks.name: Cơm gà Bà Buội
picks.what: Hội An chicken rice at 22 Phan Châu Trinh. Locals' favourite.
picks.map: Com Ga Ba Buoi Hoi An

picks.name: Night market on An Hội
picks.what: Across the bridge from the Old Town. Lanterns, snacks, and the riverside bars where everyone ends up.

picks.name: Faifo Coffee rooftop
picks.what: Probably the café you saw on YouTube: the rooftop looking over the Old Town's yellow walls and tiles. 130 Trần Phú. Get there early for a spot at the rail.

picks.name: Hoi An Roastery and Cocobox
picks.what: If Faifo's packed: both have rooftops over the Old Town too. Cocobox's only fits about ten.

tips: The Old Town is quietest before 9am and after dark.
Haggle at the tailors and the markets, but not at restaurants.

picks.name: Surf My Khe
picks.what: January and February are when Đà Nẵng actually gets swell. Two-hour lessons, or rent a board from the surf shacks on the beach.

picks.name: Hải Vân Pass
picks.what: The coastal mountain road Top Gear made famous. Scooter up from Đà Nẵng for the views, back by lunch.

picks.name: Sơn Trà Peninsula
picks.what: Ride round to the giant Lady Buddha at Linh Ứng Pagoda and look for the rare red-shanked monkeys in the trees.

picks.name: Fishing and snorkelling boat
picks.what: Half-day speedboat trip off Sơn Trà with a stop at a fishing village.

picks.name: Marble Mountains
picks.what: Limestone hills full of caves and pagodas. Climb to the top for a view down the coast.

picks.name: Bà Nà Hills and the Golden Bridge
picks.what: Expensive and touristy theme park up a mountain, but it's where the giant stone hands are. Only worth it if you're there by 7am.

picks.name: Mì Quảng Bà Mua
picks.what: The central Vietnam noodle dish, with pork, shrimp and crackers. 19 Trần Bình Trọng.

picks.name: Bánh xèo Bà Dưỡng
picks.what: Crispy pancakes wrapped in mustard leaves, with a peanut-and-liver dipping sauce. Down an alley off Hoàng Diệu.

picks.name: Bé Mặn seafood
picks.what: No-frills, pick-from-the-tank seafood that's fresh and cheap. Check the address on Maps, sources disagree.

picks.name: Dragon Bridge fire show
picks.what: The bridge breathes fire and water at 9pm on weekends. You're there Sat 30 and Sun 31 Jan.

picks.name: An Thượng
picks.what: The streets behind My Khe Beach. Bars, pubs and late food, where the backpackers and expats go out.

picks.name: Sơn Trà night market
picks.what: 150-odd food stalls. Grab dinner here on the night of a fire show.

picks.name: Golden Bridge hands
picks.what: The bridge held up by two giant stone hands.

tips: Tết prep kicks off while you're here: flower markets, decorations, traffic. It's a great time to be in a city.
Rent scooters by the week. It's cheaper than by the day.

days.title: Tết, day one
items: Sleep in
Walk the empty Old Quarter
Trấn Quốc Pagoda on West Lake with the families

picks.name: New Year's Eve fireworks at Hoàn Kiếm Lake
picks.what: Midnight on Friday 5 Feb. Streets round the lake are packed by 9pm and roads close from the afternoon. Or book a table at a lakeside café balcony.

picks.name: Hàng Lược flower market
picks.what: The Old Quarter's Tết flower market: peach blossom, kumquat trees, everyone hauling them home on motorbikes. It runs right up to New Year's Eve.

picks.name: First day of Tết
picks.what: Sat 6 Feb. The city empties and families head to the pagodas. Walk the silent Old Quarter, then go to Trấn Quốc Pagoda on West Lake.

picks.name: Calligraphy at the Temple of Literature
picks.what: Calligraphers set up around Tết. Ask for a character for luck to take home.

picks.name: The Instagram tour guy
picks.what: Book for 4 Feb, before Tết closures.

picks.name: Train Street
picks.what: Cafés a foot from the tracks. The city cut back the trains in 2026, so check they're still running before you go.

picks.name: Bún chả
picks.what: Grilled pork, noodles and herbs in a sweet-sour broth. Hương Liên (24 Lê Văn Hưu) is the Obama one. Đắc Kim (1 Hàng Mành) is better value.

picks.name: Egg coffee at Café Giang
picks.what: Where egg coffee was invented. 39 Nguyễn Hữu Huân, cash only.

picks.name: Phở Gia Truyền, 49 Bát Đàn
picks.what: The phở with the queue down the street. Order, pay, carry your own bowl.

picks.name: Tạ Hiện beer street
picks.what: Bia hơi on plastic stools. May be quieter over Tết, but you'll get it properly on your last night.

tips: From about 6 to 8 Feb lots of street stalls and small shops shut. Hotels and bigger restaurants stay open.
Grab adds a Tết surcharge of about ₫10–30k per ride.
Say 'Chúc mừng năm mới' to everyone. You'll get big smiles.

Bikes out to Bích Động Pagoda
Goat for dinner

Thung Nham bird valley at dusk

days.title: Rest, then north
items: Lazy morning
Overnight drive to Hà Giang

picks.name: Hang Múa viewpoint
picks.what: About 500 steps up to a stone dragon on the ridge with the whole valley below. Go at sunrise or sunset.

picks.name: Tràng An boat trip
picks.what: The UNESCO one: 2–3 hours rowed through caves under the mountains. At Tết, be on the water by 7am.

picks.name: Tam Cốc boat
picks.what: Shorter and more rustic, and the rowers use their feet. Vendors paddle up to sell snacks, so just say no thanks.

picks.name: Cycle the rice fields
picks.what: Hire bikes from the homestay and ride out to Bích Động Pagoda in the late afternoon.

picks.name: Thung Nham bird valley
picks.what: Thousands of birds come back to roost at dusk.

picks.name: Mountain goat
picks.what: Ninh Bình's thing: dê tái chanh (goat with lime) and goat hot pot. Quán Dê Thanh Cao on Lê Lợi does the real stuff.

picks.name: Cơm cháy
picks.what: Crispy rice crackers with a goat or beef sauce poured over.

picks.name: Tam Cốc main street
picks.what: A few bars and a craft-beer place.

tips: Pick two big things a day at most, or you'll spend the whole time on the road.
Skip Bái Đính Pagoda over Tết unless you love crowds.

picks.name: Mã Pí Lèng Pass and the Nho Quế River
picks.what: The most photographed road in the north, then a boat down the emerald river through the Tu Sản canyon below it.

picks.name: Heaven's Gate, Quản Bạ
picks.what: First big viewpoint on day one, over the 'Twin Mountains'.

picks.name: Lũng Cú Flag Tower
picks.what: Vietnam's northernmost point, right on the China border.

picks.name: Đồng Văn Old Town
picks.what: Stone houses and the old quarter. If you're there on Sunday 14 Feb, catch the market.

picks.name: Du Già waterfall
picks.what: Swimming hole at the usual last stop. It'll be freezing in February.

picks.name: Homestay nights
picks.what: Dinner with the riders, 'happy water' (homemade corn wine) and karaoke.

tips: February is 8–18°C, and much colder on the passes. Thermals, gloves and a neck warmer.
Bring cash. There are almost no ATMs past the first day.

Board the cruise or settle in on Cát Bà

days.title: Kayaks and caves
items: Kayak through the lagoons
Caves and a swim if it's warm enough

days.title: Cát Bà or another day on the water
items: Hike the national park or climb Cannon Fort

days.title: Back to Hà Nội
items: Transfer back, about 2.5 hours

picks.name: Overnight cruise
picks.what: Bái Tử Long is the quietest, with only a few boats. Lan Hạ (via Cát Bà) has the most choice and a younger crowd. Either beats the main Hạ Long route.
picks.price: about US$110–150 each, 2 days and 1 night

picks.name: Kayaking the lagoons
picks.what: Paddle under rock arches into hidden lagoons. Usually included on the cruise.

picks.name: Cát Bà Island
picks.what: If you want a land base: hike the national park, climb Cannon Fort, and take day boats into Lan Hạ.

picks.name: Chả mực
picks.what: Hạ Long's famous squid cakes. Have them with sticky rice.

tips: February mornings are often misty. It burns off and it looks moody in photos, and cruises rarely get cancelled.
Book a cruise that includes the Hà Nội transfer.

days.title: Last night
items: Bia hơi on Tạ Hiện
A speakeasy to finish
Last bún chả at whichever one won

picks.name: Bia hơi on Tạ Hiện
picks.what: Fresh beer on plastic stools.

picks.name: A proper speakeasy
picks.what: Hà Nội's cocktail scene is good. Kumquat Tree made the World's 50 Best discovery list.

picks.name: Last bún chả
picks.what: Hương Liên or Đắc Kim.

picks.name: Coffee to take home
picks.what: Vietnamese coffee and a phin filter make a great cheap present.

tips: The airport is about 45 minutes by Grab. Leave plenty of time.

rules.title: Tết manners
rules.text: Wish people 'Chúc mừng năm mới'. Don't wear all black or all white (they're for mourning), and don't argue or break things on the first day. If you're invited to someone's home, bring fruit or sweets.

rules.title: Money
rules.text: The ₫20,000 and ₫500,000 notes are both blue. Check before you hand one over. Street food is cash only. Haggle at markets, not in restaurants.

rules.title: Getting around
rules.text: Use Grab for cars and bikes; the price is fixed up front. Always wear the helmet.

rules.title: Phones
rules.text: Bag snatchers on motorbikes work the busy streets in Sài Gòn. Hold your phone away from the road.
